summary.headline: Kellton Q4 FY26 revenue about Rs 319-320 crore with 9.8% EBITDA margin; FY26 revenue up about 11.4% YoY to Rs 1,225 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue of about Rs 319-320 crore, EBITDA of Rs 30.7 crore (9.8% margin) and PAT of Rs 19.5 crore. For FY26, revenue was Rs 1,225 crore (up about 11.4% YoY), EBITDA about Rs 143-144 crore and PAT Rs 91 crore. Management flagged that Q4 is a balancing quarter with audit-driven regrouping, so figures may not be comparable with earlier published numbers. The U.S. business is growing steadily but slower than expected, with receivable slowdowns and AI-related deal delays linked to the war-related economic uncertainty.

financial_highlights.change: Affected by increase in share count after full conversion of FCCB
EBITDA margin stated as 1.8% for the full year (figure as spoken, appears inconsistent with the EBITDA amount)
Affected by increase in share count after full FCCB conversion

segments.name: U.S. business
segments.commentary: Growing steadily but below expectations, with slower accounts receivable collections as customers hold payments amid war uncertainty. AI-led deals are stalling at contract-signing or project-start stage.

segments.name: India / AI products
segments.commentary: Phoenix.ai legacy modernization framework claims above 80% automated code conversion versus 20-30% from market tools; a 4 million line ERP conversion is underway. Structy.ai data framework was announced with a global consulting firm.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target of about 10%, with more than 10% possible if conditions are favourable (answer given to an individual investor's question on the year-end target, which was framed around FY26 revenue growth; treat as management's stated view).
Management expects AI-led deal starts to pick up in the next quarter or so if the U.S.-Iran situation eases.
Expects revenue from Microsoft and ServiceNow partnerships, and Snowflake data/AI practice, to grow this year after a small base last year.
Says the journey B2B travel platform's initial 18-month estimate has been compressed, with 80% of the solution expected in one quarter using AI tooling.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity, or utilisation figures were discussed on the call.
Kumori (acquired for ServiceNow capability) is being used to target U.S. ServiceNow demand; only one quarter of contribution so far.
Management said acquisitions are considered for customers, geographic reach or capability, not for top-line contribution; no specific deal was announced.
demand_pricing: Client inquiries for AI enablement of core systems are high, but signings and project kick-offs are being delayed by the war-related uncertainty.

Six client wins were cited: a travel technology platform (cloud-native integration), a global financial payments enterprise (application modernisation), a major private bank (AI video KYC), a global engineering/consulting firm (ServiceNow accounting center), a cyber technology company (ServiceNow CMDB), and a global technology enterprise (ServiceNow orchestration and analytics).
Management cited a market benchmark of $1-2 per line of code for legacy code conversion, versus Kellton's Phoenix.ai framework on a 4 million line project.
Customers in the U.S. are asking how AI efficiencies are being built into delivery; larger enterprises are at planning stage.

qa_highlights.question: How has Kumori performed post-acquisition, and are synergies visible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kumori is growing and gave Kellton ServiceNow partnership depth. Three partnerships (Microsoft, ServiceNow, Snowflake) are targeted as the next growth phase; Microsoft is already generating revenue and ServiceNow is now being targeted in the U.S. after only one quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY-end revenue target?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth of about 10% for the year, with more than 10% possible if everything goes right.

qa_highlights.question: How is the U.S. business trending, and are acquisitions planned?
qa_highlights.answer: U.S. business is growing steadily but below expectations due to war uncertainty and AI-driven efficiency expectations; receivables have slowed, with management expecting normalisation within about 60 days. Acquisitions are screened for customers, geography or capability, not top-line.

qa_highlights.question: How is AI being adopted internally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI is used in QA, product management and development (Copilot standardised, Claude now leading), and customers are asking how Kellton uses AI in its own SDLC and approving AI tool licences on T&M engagements.

risks_watch: Q4 is an audit balancing quarter; regrouping of prior-quarter provisions and allotments may change comparatives.
U.S. receivables slowdown; watch DSO and collections over the next 60 days.
AI-led and U.S. deal signings delayed by war-related uncertainty; management expects pickup in about one quarter but this is contingent on geopolitical easing.
Increased share count after full FCCB conversion dilutes per-share figures; EPS comparability is affected.
FY26 EBITDA margin figure stated as 1.8% does not reconcile with Rs 143-144 crore EBITDA on Rs 1,225 crore revenue; clarification needed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on AI capability and the pipeline, but cautious on near-term U.S. demand, which management attributes to the war and AI-driven deal delays. Figures were presented with several caveats about audit regrouping and EPS base effects.
key_quotes: Revenue, we are looking at (+10%) growth for this year is what we are looking at. If everything goes our way, it could be more than 10%.

The war has put some uncertainty on the economy. And because of that, at the final stages when all the contract negotiations have happened, initiating or kick -starting the project is where the delays are happening.
So, it's almost 80% to 90% of the code that gets converted is automated using this agent.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of about 10%, with more than 10% possible if conditions are favourable, but gives no capacity, order-book or contract numbers behind it, and says AI deal starts are stalled by war-related uncertainty.
